name: Mở đầu: Phép loại suy kịch bản (Script Analogy)
text: Imagine you happen across a short movie script describing a scene between a person and their AI assistant. The script has what the person asks, but the AI's response has been torn off. Suppose you also have a powerful magical machine that can take any text and provide a sensible prediction of what word comes next. You could finish the script by feeding in what you have, seeing what it predicts to start the AI's answer, and repeating this over and over, completing the dialogue. When you interact with a chatbot, this is exactly what's happening. A Large Language Model is a sophisticated mathematical function that predicts what word comes next for any piece of text. Instead of predicting one word with certainty, it assigns a probability to all possible next words.

name: Xây dựng một chatbot
text: To build a chatbot, you lay out some text describing an interaction between a user and a hypothetical AI assistant. You add on whatever the user types as the first part, then have the model repeatedly predict the next word that such an AI assistant would say. In doing this, the output looks more natural if you allow it to select less likely words at random. So even though the model itself is deterministic, a given prompt typically gives a different answer each time it's run.

name: Quy mô huấn luyện (Scale of Training)
text: Models learn to make these predictions by processing an enormous amount of text, typically pulled from the internet. For a standard human to read the amount of text used to train GPT-3, reading non-stop 24/7, it would take over 2,600 years. Larger models since then train on much, much more.

name: Tham số và Trọng số (Parameters & Weights)
text: You can think of training a bit like tuning the dials on a big machine. The way a language model behaves is entirely determined by these many continuous values, usually called parameters or weights. Changing those parameters changes the probabilities the model gives for the next word. What puts the 'Large' in Large Language Model is how they can have hundreds of billions of these parameters. No human ever deliberately sets them. They begin at random, so the model just outputs gibberish, but they're repeatedly refined based on many example pieces of text.

name: Quá trình huấn luyện: Backpropagation
text: One training example could be a handful of words, or thousands. Either way, you pass in all but the last word from that example into the model and compare its prediction with the true last word. An algorithm called backpropagation tweaks all the parameters so the model is a little more likely to choose the true last word and a little less likely to choose the others. Do this for many trillions of examples, and the model starts to give accurate predictions even on text it's never seen before.

name: Quy mô tính toán (Scale of Computation)
text: The scale of computation involved in training a large language model is mind-boggling. Imagine you could perform one billion additions and multiplications every single second. How long would it take to do all the operations involved in training the largest language models? A year? 10,000 years? The answer is well over 100 million years.

name: RLHF: Tinh chỉnh để trở thành trợ lý
text: This is only part of the story. This whole process is called pre-training. The goal of auto-completing a random passage from the internet is very different from being a good AI assistant. To address this, chatbots undergo another type of training called Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF). Workers flag unhelpful or problematic predictions, and their corrections further change the model's parameters, making it more likely to give predictions users prefer.

name: Kiến trúc Transformer
text: This staggering amount of computation is only made possible by special computer chips optimized for running many operations in parallel, known as GPUs. But not all language models can be easily parallelized. Prior to 2017, most language models processed text one word at a time. Then a team at Google introduced a new model known as the Transformer. Transformers don't read text start to finish; they soak it all in at once, in parallel. The first step inside a transformer is to associate each word with a long list of numbers, because the training process only works with continuous values, and each list of numbers may somehow encode the meaning of the word.

name: Attention và Feedforward
text: What makes Transformers unique is their reliance on a special operation known as Attention. This gives all of these lists of numbers a chance to talk to one another and refine the meanings they encode based on the context around them, all in parallel. For example, the numbers encoding 'bank' might change based on context to encode the notion of a 'river bank'. Transformers also include a feedforward neural network, giving the model extra capacity to store more patterns about language. All this data repeatedly flows through many iterations of these two operations, so each list of numbers is enriched to encode whatever is needed to predict the next word.

name: Kết: Hiện tượng phát sinh (Emergent)
text: At the end, one final function is performed on the last vector to produce a prediction of the next word, again a probability for every possible next word. Although researchers design the framework for how each step works, the specific behavior is an emergent phenomenon based on how those hundreds of billions of parameters are tuned during training. This makes it incredibly challenging to determine why the model makes the exact predictions it does. What you can see is that the words it generates are uncannily fluent, fascinating, and even useful.
